spark.scene: True-color satellite view of the Hawaiian island chain stretching northwest to southeast over dark ocean with scattered bright white cumulus and thin cirrus. The large southeastern island is partly cloud-covered with a diffuse gray veil visible over the ocean to its west.

plumes.visual_description: diffuse translucent gray veil over ocean to the west of the large southeastern island, grayer and more uniform than surrounding bright white cumulus clouds

track.note: Centroid drift of a plume still attached to its source is slower than the air; direction is the main signal, speed is approximate.

per_plume.source_hint: Kilauea summit; ENE trades carry emissions WSW over ocean west of Hawaii island
evidence: Kilauea was active with intermittent north-vent overflows through the image day (WATCH/ORANGE), while Mauna Loa was NORMAL/GREEN and not erupting, favoring Kilauea as the vog source. [E1]

Wind from 74 deg (ENE, 29.6 km/h) blows toward ~254 deg (WSW); measured plume drift toward 258 deg at 30.9 km/h with fit R2 0.93 agrees within ~4 deg and matches speed, supporting WSW transport west of Hawaii island. [E2, E4]
No FIRMS fire clusters in the region on 2026-10-15, ruling against wildfire smoke; 28 volcanic-thermal pixels at Kilauea summit confirm active summit heat. [E7]
Mask is 100% over ocean (land_frac 0.0) west of the large island, consistent with transported gray veil distinct from bright white cumulus over land/islands. [E3]

Geometry is large diffuse veil (4043 km2, 112 km long) with upwind end at 19.925N 156.37W, 127.6 km from Kilauea and 94.2 km from Mauna Loa, and tracked source end similarly distant, indicating aged/detached vog rather than vent-attached plume. [E6, E4]

classify.caveats: Plume is detached: upwind/eastern end remains >90 km from both summits, so vent attribution relies on wind transport and eruption status rather than contiguity. Faint diffuse veil could contain thin cloud haze mixture.

kilauea.activity_summary: Intermittent overflows from the north vent resumed yesterday and continued through day; less frequent overnight. Kīlauea's summit remains at a high level of pressurization with changes in eruptive activity or location within the summit region possible.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
